messages:
sam: Quick check — hitting intermittent 401s on streaming reconnects when using service account JWTs. Happens after ~30s of idle, only for a subset of requests. Anyone seen this with project-scoped aud/iss?

maria: Hmm, do you mean you're minting a JWT with aud set to the private endpoint URL, then exchanging for an OIDC token? :thinking:

sam: Yeah. Flow is: create JWT (svc acct), sign, POST to /v1/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt, get back id_token then use that for the websocket auth header. 401s on reconnect only.

adrien: Any logs from the auth service? Usually 401 on reconnect implies either token expired or aud mismatch on the second handshake. Could be caching issue where we accidentally validate old aud after rotation.

tim: Also check clock skew on the machine minting the JWT. If exp/nbf are off by a few secs the initial connection may work (due to grace) but revalidate fails.

maria: Can you paste the JWT payload (redacted)? Also which SDK/lang are you using — node/python/rust? Different clients sometimes drop the new token when reattaching stream.

sam: Using node@16 SDK (official). Payload looks like: ```{ "iss": "svc-account@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com", "sub": "svc-account@project", "aud": "https://private.redwood/api", "iat": 1670000000, "exp": 1670000360, "projects": ["project-a"] }``` (redacted).

adrien: Quick note — exp only 360s. On stream reconnects the client may attempt to reuse a cached token if reconnect happens >60s after connect. Try increasing exp to 1h-ish for streaming or implement short-lived exchange for each reconnect.

maria: Also confirm the SDK's reauth hook is actually swapping the header. There's a known issue in node-sdk v0.9.3 where reconnect path uses internal cached headers unless you pass `reauth: true` into the stream options. Which SDK version?

sam: We're on v0.9.3. Oof. Can repro locally by forcing a reconnect after 45s.

tim: Two quick mitigations: 1) bump jwt exp to 3600, 2) upgrade node-sdk to 0.9.5 (fixes header refresh on reconnect). Both can be temporary.

adrien: For long-term I'd recommend switching to the OIDC client flow that exchanges JWT -> access_token with TTL aligned to stream lifecycle and use token refresh handler on `onReconnect`. Example snippet for node:
```js
const client = new RedwoodStream({ reauth: () => getFreshToken(), ... });
client.on('reconnect', async () => { await client.setAuth(await getFreshToken()); });
```

maria: Also a heads-up on scoping: if you mint a JWT scoped to a specific GCP project (aud contains project) but the private endpoint validates org-level aud, you'll get inconsistent acceptances depending on route. Make aud match the token validator config.

sam: Thanks — upgrading to 0.9.5 + increasing exp fixed the repro in dev. I'll roll a canary.

devex-bot: deploy: canary for svcacct/streaming-auth-rollout started by @sam — watch logs at https://console.redwood/dev/streams/canary (alerts enabled). :rocket:

maria: ping me if the canary shows non-401 regressions. I can run a quick fuzz of different aud values/claims.

sam: Will do, thx everyone. If the canary looks good, I'll open a PR to bump SDK and add a test for reconnect header refresh.

adrien: Thanks — can you also add a short blurb in the SDK changelog about `reauth` behavior so integrators know to increase exp or call refresh?

sam: Yep, will include that in PR description and add an integration test.

tim: Nice. If you want a quick code review ping me in the PR thread. :thumbsup:
